newsitem.title: UK: Two Brent cargoes trade lower, CFDs fall sharply.
newsitem.headline: Two Brent cargoes trade lower, CFDs fall sharply.

text.p: Two cargoes of March loading Brent crude oil traded on Monday at numbers that continued to reflect the downward pressure on the market from an excess supply of prompt North Sea barrels, traders said.
A March 27-29 Brent sold at April Brent -80 cents for a maximum sized cargo and a March 26-28 moved at April Brent -81 cents. Next highest bids were about April -90 cents, sellers said.

The CFD market dropped sharply in reaction to the deals with this week offered at May -50 cents and bid 10 cents lower. March 24-27, traded earlier at May -32 cents, was offered around May -35 cents, brokers said.
"This market is going back into contango," one North Sea equity holder said.
Brent May/June, which traded earlier at +13 cents, was now offered at +10 cents with the strongest bid three cents lower.
"The market is perfectly set up to go into contango. If the outright price goes down I think we will do it," another North Sea player said.
There were two Brent cargoes in the paper chains on Monday.
The April Ekofisk programme, released in the morning, held few surprises gaining two cargoes on the month to 33 cargoes.

The lower than expected April loading programme for Brent did little to change traders views that oversupply in the sweet North Sea market would continue into next month. The April Brent programme, released on Friday, was down eight cargoes on the month at 35 cargoes.
